Why does a steady worker still need a queue?

Yellow = waiting. Green = done this tick. The drawing is the argument; the caption is one line.

—peak items waiting
0requests dropped
A queue buys time, not throughput. If the burst never ends, no queue size saves you — only a faster worker does.
The "words" panel is for the reader who wants prose. It is hidden until they press w, so the default view stays visual. Put nuance, caveats and the second-order detail here, never in the drawing.
Source: your measurement, paper or code path · path/to/file.py:42
  1. A burst arrives: six requests in the time the worker can finish one.
  2. The queue holds what the worker cannot take yet — nothing is thrown away.
  3. The worker drains at its own rate, tick after tick, never faster.
  4. What you must size is the peak, and the peak is burst minus rate — not the average.
